Evidence: No 1E event cards exist (Core p.6–7 lists none). V2 p.6/p.19 has 30 un-levelled event cards of three kinds (Immediate, Consumable, Rendezvous) drawn after completing an encounter. The manuscript lists levelled event cards plus 'Special Trap cards', deals one per tile, reveals it at encounter start and allows scrying it, but contains no rule stating what an event card does.
Current text: 10x Level 1 event cards / 10x Level 2 event cards / 10x Level 3 event cards / 5x Special Trap cards … Deal one face-down event card of the encounter card's level to each tile … Reveal the tile's event card, if not already revealed.
Proposed fix: Either (a) add a section 'Event Cards' defining the card anatomy, when the card's text applies, and how it is discarded or reset when the characters rest; or (b) delete every reference to event cards (components, setup steps 3 and 7, encounter start step 5, event scrying).
Rationale: A V2-style component has been grafted onto 1E tiles with no mechanic attached; the halves are not reconciled because the V2 event mechanic (drawn after an encounter, tied to the encounter track) cannot operate in the manuscript's tile dungeon.
Gameplay impact: Players cannot resolve setup or encounter start as written.

Evidence: PH p.8: 'there will be a summon activation after each character activation' (boss, character, summon, boss, character, summon). The manuscript's phantom acts 'after all character turns are resolved and before the first enemy turn begins', a phase that exists only in the manuscript's round-based standard encounters (1281–1295); boss encounters keep the 1E alternation (2158), where no such phase occurs.
Current text: Phantoms take their turn after all character turns are resolved and before the first enemy turn begins.
Proposed fix: The phantom takes a turn immediately after each character's turn, before the boss's next turn. The phantom does not take a turn after the boss's turn.
Rationale: The summon cadence was written for the manuscript's round structure, but summons appear only in boss encounters, which use 1E alternation. The official cadence (PH p.8) fits boss alternation without further change.
Gameplay impact: As written the phantom never has a defined moment to act in a boss fight.

Evidence: 1E gravestone tokens are single-sided (Core p.7, p.17). V2 p.12 gravestones have illuminated and diminished sides and are flipped after use. The manuscript adopts V2 scrying but never flips a gravestone; the sentence about not flipping is a vestige of V2.
Current text: When the characters rest at the bonfire, gravestone tokens are not flipped from their current side or moved.
Proposed fix: When the characters rest at the bonfire, gravestone tokens are not moved.
Rationale: Removes a reference to a state the manuscript's gravestones never enter.

Evidence: Core p.28 says a character pushed off a boss's node must remain in the same arc. FAQ p.1 overrides this: 'Any time a character is pushed by an attack, it simply needs to be moved farther from the attacking model (p. 21).' The manuscript keeps the pre-FAQ text and adds an original 'centre-most node' clause.
Current text: If the character is pushed off of the boss's base arc, they must move to the centre-most node in the boss's arc they originate from, if possible. Otherwise, the character is pushed to any valid node in that arc.
Proposed fix: If a character is pushed off a boss's node by an attack, the character moves to an adjacent node farther from the boss; the arc restriction does not apply. If a character is pushed off a boss's node by the boss's movement, the character moves to a node within the arc the character occupied.
Rationale: The official FAQ ruling distinguishes attack pushes from movement pushes; the manuscript's version follows the superseded rulebook text.

Evidence: Core p.15 basic game has three tiers (2/4/8). Core p.33 campaign adds tier 4 at 20 souls with a value of 40. HE p.5 has 2/4/6/8 with tier 4 = 40 stat points marked by a red cube. The manuscript charges 8 for tier three and 8 for tier four and defines tier four as 'considered 5 greater than the tier three stat value'.
Current text: Tier Three 8 / Tier Four 8 … Tier four stats are all considered 5 greater than the tier three stat value.
Proposed fix: Tier Four: 12 souls. A stat at tier four has a value of 40.
Rationale: The red-cube marker is HE; the cost column is 1E with a duplicated 8; the '+5' value matches neither source and produces different tier-four values per class and per stat. The 40 value is shared by 1E campaign and HE and is already used by the manuscript's own campaign table (20 souls, Core p.33).
Gameplay impact: Equip thresholds at 35–40 differ by class under the '+5' rule.

Evidence: Official card types are starting, common, class, transposed, legendary, boss (Core p.12); slots are one-handed, two-handed, armour (V2 p.10). 'Shield' and 'spell' are not card types; several shields carry attack options and spells occupy weapon slots. The stocking formula cannot be applied to a card deterministically.
Current text: 3 weapons, 3 armour, 2 shields, 2 upgrades, and 2 spells.
Proposed fix: For shop stocking a card is classed in the first matching category: upgrade (upgrade icon); spell (scroll art); shield (weapon-slot card with a block or resist value and no attack dice); armour (armour icon); weapon (any other weapon-slot card). Draw cards until each category is filled; set aside cards of a filled category and shuffle them back afterwards.
Rationale: The fixed-composition shop is original to the manuscript and replaces the 1E blind draw and the V2 four-card display; it needs a classification rule for the official card pool.
Gameplay impact: Shop stocking is the game's main equipment source.

Evidence: BDK/EC p.10 apply the standard boss rules (party defeated → rest at the bonfire, spark spent). The manuscript's Objective says the players lose only when all characters are dead and no sparks remain, but the mega-boss step says a character who dies is permanently removed and all dead = loss regardless of sparks.
Current text: If a character dies they are permanently removed from play. If all characters die, the players lose the game.
Proposed fix: A character who dies in the mega-boss encounter is removed from play for the remainder of that encounter. If every character dies, the encounter is failed and the characters rest at the bonfire at the cost of one spark; the mega-boss encounter is then set up again.
Rationale: Reconciles the mega-boss rule with the manuscript's own loss condition and with the official mega-boss booklets; the alternative is to keep sudden death and amend the Objective.
Gameplay impact: Decides whether sparks matter in the final fight.

Evidence: Core p.25 defines enemy attack targeting: skull icon = character with the aggro token, ring icon = nearest character (ties → aggro, then higher taunt); an attack whose target is out of range misses; the Node icon attacks every character on the target's node, each rolling separately. V2 p.25 repeats this. The manuscript explains these icons only for movement (1672–1694) and says attack modifiers are 'detailed later', but no such section exists.
Current text: Additional symbols beside the attack type icon modify the attack with special rules detailed later.
Proposed fix: An attack with the skull icon targets the character with the aggro token. An attack with the ring icon targets the nearest character; if two or more characters are tied for nearest, the attack targets the one with the aggro token, and otherwise the tied character with the higher threat level. If the target is not within the attack's range, the attack misses and has no effect. An attack with the node icon targets every character on the target's node; each defends separately.
Rationale: Silently dropped from Core p.25 while the movement half of the same page was copied; without it an enemy turn cannot be resolved.

Evidence: Core p.18: on revealing a trap the character 'must suffer the damage or attempt to dodge'; trap damage cannot be blocked; traps have no effect on enemies and cannot be triggered by them; a trap triggers once per encounter. V2 p.12: defence roll with dodge dice only. The manuscript says only 'resolve its effect on all models on that node', which both omits the resolution procedure and implies enemies are affected.
Current text: When a character is pushed onto or moves into a node containing a face-down trap token, flip the token face-up and resolve its effect on all models on that node.
Proposed fix: When a character moves or is pushed onto a node containing a face-down trap token, flip the token. A blank token has no effect. Otherwise each character on that node either suffers the damage shown or attempts to dodge against the dodge difficulty shown; trap damage cannot be blocked or resisted. Enemies are not affected by traps and do not trigger them. A face-up trap token has no further effect during that encounter.
Rationale: Restores the official resolution; the manuscript's 'all models' wording is the only part that needs a decision (whether enemies suffer traps).
Gameplay impact: Trapped encounters are unplayable without a resolution rule.

Evidence: PH p.6: summons have a taunt level, block/resist/dodge values and a special ability; p.9: the Distract icon makes the summon count as holding the aggro token for the next boss activation; summon death does not force a rest. None of these appear in the manuscript, which also calls the behaviour card an 'encounter card' (1991).
Current text: Draw a random phantom card of appropriate level … After each icon on the encounter card is resolved in left to right order, the phantom's turn ends.
Proposed fix: A phantom defends with its own block, resist and dodge values and is targeted by enemies using its threat level as if it were a character. When a behaviour shows the distract icon, the phantom is treated as holding the aggro token during the boss's next turn; the token itself is not moved. The phantom's special ability applies as printed on its data card. A phantom's death has no effect on the characters.
Rationale: The manuscript adopts the Phantoms expansion components but omits the rules that make the summon data card usable.
Gameplay impact: Boss targeting with a summon present is undefined.

Evidence: Core p.15: 'A character must spend 1 soul to flip their Luck token to the ready side' at the Firekeeper. The manuscript restores luck only by resting (1901) and gives no replacement.
Current text: (absent)
Proposed fix: At the Firekeeper a character may pay one soul to flip their luck token to the ready side.
Rationale: Probably an intentional drop (luck is stronger in the manuscript, rerolling any number of dice), but it is not acknowledged; the author decides.

Location: manuscript.md 2366–2368 and 2468–2470 (The First Journey; Ambush Lies Ahead, Section One)
Evidence: Core p.35 and PH p.17 footnote: the party receives the Gargoyles' treasure only after defeating two Gargoyle encounters back-to-back; if defeated by the second, both must be fought again from the Fog Gate.
Current text: Gargoyle (Mini-Boss) / Gargoyle (Mini-Boss)
Proposed fix: The characters receive the Gargoyle treasure only after defeating two Gargoyle encounters in succession. If the second Gargoyle defeats the party, both Gargoyle encounters are fought again.
Rationale: The two listed Gargoyle entries are meaningless without the footnote.
Gameplay impact: Campaign section one cannot be resolved.

Evidence: EC p.18: encounter cards are never turned face down when the party rests; a defeated encounter is never fought again; the party gains 4 souls per player per encounter regardless of level; sections 5 and 6 each contain a Level 4 encounter drawn from the Vordt/Chariot decks. The manuscript lists the sections but omits all three special rules and the Level 4 encounter of section six.
Current text: Section Six - Terror of the Ring: Bonfire Tile / Level 3 Encounter - Desolate Cemetery / Vordt of the Boreal Valley (Mega Boss)
Proposed fix: Section Six: Bonfire Tile; Level 3 Encounter – Desolate Cemetery; Level 4 Encounter; Vordt of the Boreal Valley (Mega Boss). In this campaign cleared encounters are not reset when the characters rest and are never fought again; each cleared encounter rewards four souls per character irrespective of its level.
Rationale: The campaign's identity is its no-reset rule; without it the listing is just a longer standard campaign.

Evidence: BDK/EC p.8: in a level 4 encounter all four nodes along the wall beside the doorway are entry nodes. BDK/EC p.9: the fog gate is placed on the doorway only after the level 4 encounter is cleared and the board is flipped. The manuscript places the fog gate before the level 4 encounter and says nothing about entry nodes.
Current text: Place the Level 4 encounter tile associated with the chosen mega-boss adjacent to The Bonfire tile with the fog-gate placed at the entrance.
Proposed fix: Place the level 4 encounter tile, encounter side up, adjacent to the bonfire tile. All four nodes along the wall beside the doorway are entry nodes. After the level 4 encounter is cleared, flip the tile to its mega-boss side and place the fog gate on its doorway.
Rationale: Aligns with the mega-boss booklets; the fog gate timing matters because the manuscript's fog-gate shortcut (2066) triggers on first passage.

Location: manuscript.md 1113–1117 (Encounter tiles) and 1152 (Setup After the mini-boss)
Evidence: Core p.8 step 1: 'Take the Fog Gate token and place it on an empty portion of a wall on the tile farthest from the Bonfire tile.' The manuscript's initial tile setup never places the fog gate; step 4 after the mini-boss says 'Place the fog-gate as before', referring to a step that does not exist.
Current text: Arrange the doorways of the encounter tiles so there are two open doorways that connect to an adjacent tile. This will create a linear route along four sequential encounter tiles between bonfire and boss tiles.
Proposed fix: Place the fog gate token on the doorway between the fourth encounter tile and the boss tile.
Rationale: The fog gate drives the manuscript's shortcut rule (2066) and campaign note (2230); its initial placement is a dropped official setup step.
Gameplay impact: Setup cannot be completed as written.

Evidence: FAQ p.1: a movement attack 'only targets all characters on each node the enemy moves into' — characters on the enemy's starting node are moved but not damaged. The manuscript moves them first (1594) and then says all pushed characters suffer the damage (1702), leaving the starting node ambiguous.
Current text: If the push icon includes a number, characters pushed out of the way suffer that amount of damage during the push.
Proposed fix: Characters moved from the enemy's starting node suffer no damage. Each character on a node the enemy moves onto is pushed and suffers the damage shown; the damage may be blocked or dodged.
Rationale: Adopts the FAQ ruling the manuscript otherwise follows (1596).

Evidence: Core p.22: 'a character may move before attacking or after attacking (but not both)'. V2 p.20: move then action or action then move. HE p.9: 'Actions can be done in any order.' The manuscript lists minor actions joined by AND and major actions joined by OR without stating whether minor actions may be taken both before and after the major action.
Current text: Minor Actions: Walk AND Run AND Equip AND Heroic Action. Major Action: Attack OR Rest OR Drink Estus OR Ember.
Proposed fix: During a character's turn, minor actions and the major action may be taken in any order; each minor action may be taken once, except run, which may be repeated.
Rationale: The manuscript's action economy is HE-derived; HE's free ordering is the natural completion, but the 1E restriction is equally coherent and changes hit-and-run tactics, so the author decides.
Gameplay impact: Whether a character can walk, attack, then run away.

Evidence: Core p.7 lists 1x First Activation Token. The manuscript's component list omits it but uses a 'first player token' (1277) and a 'first turn token' (3056).
Current text: (absent from list)
Proposed fix: 1x First Activation token
Rationale: Either list the token or delete the two references (characters act in threat order, so the token has no function outside PvP).

Evidence: EXP p.4: 2x Mimic Miniatures, 2x Mimic Data Cards (Hungry Mimic, Voracious Mimic).
Current text: 1x HungryVoracious Mimic (Explorers)
Proposed fix: 2x Mimic — Hungry Mimic and Voracious Mimic (Explorers)
Rationale: Official count is two.

Evidence: Core p.7: 5x each of Bleed, Poison, Frostbite and Stagger (20 total). BDK p.4: 4x Calamity. The manuscript states 7 of each and a total of 35, but 7×4 + 4 + 4 = 36.
Current text: 35x Condition tokens / 7x each of poison, Bleed, Stagger, and frostbite tokens / 4x each of Calamity and 4x Corrosion tokens
Proposed fix: 28x Condition tokens: 5x each of bleed, poison, frostbite and stagger (Core); 4x Calamity (Black Dragon Kalameet); 4x Corrosion (Gaping Dragon)
Rationale: The core set supplies five of each; if the extra two per condition come from another expansion the source must be named.

Evidence: Core p.20: 'If all ten of a character's endurance bar boxes have cubes, that character has been killed.' The official dashboard has ten boxes; the manuscript says eight.
Current text: The effect of these hollow markers is to reduce the functional capacity of the endurance bar from a total of eight stamina/damage cubes to only six.
Proposed fix: The hollow markers reduce the capacity of the endurance bar from ten spaces to eight.
Rationale: Factual error against the official component unless the manuscript intends custom dashboards.
Gameplay impact: Health and stamina totals for every character.

Evidence: Core p.5: one main boss, 'Dragon Slayer Ornstein & Executioner Smough', with one data card, one behaviour deck and one treasure set.
Current text: Dragonslayer Ornstein (Core) / Executioner Smough (Core)
Proposed fix: Dragonslayer Ornstein & Executioner Smough (Core)
Rationale: One boss entry, two miniatures.

Evidence: The Big Game Hunting campaign lists 'The Last Giant (Mega Boss)' (3018); The Last Giant is absent from the mega-boss component list.
Current text: (absent)
Proposed fix: The Last Giant (The Last Giant)
Rationale: A boss used by a listed campaign must appear in the component list.

Evidence: Components used by the manuscript's rules but absent from its lists: invader tokens (PH p.5: 6 standard, 6 advanced, 3 blank), 5 ambush cards (EXP p.4), 3 Titanite Scale cards (IK p.3), pillar tokens (2205), boss/summon/invader health dials, mega-boss game boards (BDK/EC p.4).
Current text: (absent)
Proposed fix: Add to the component list: 6x Standard invader tokens, 6x Advanced invader tokens, 3x Blank invader tokens (Phantoms); 5x Ambush cards (Explorers); 3x Titanite Scale cards (Iron Keep); 4x Pillar tokens (Asylum Demon); 1x Health dial per boss, summon and invader; 1x Mega-boss game board per mega-boss expansion.
Rationale: Every component referenced by a rule must be listed.

Evidence: Supplied booklets give DR 18, IK 18, EXP 15, EC 10 (incl. 4 level 4), BDK 4 level 4, ToG 29 (V2 p.6); PWA and the other mega-boss sets are not supplied. The stated 31 per level and 40 level-4 cards cannot be reconciled from the supplied sources (9 listed mega-bosses × 4 = 36).
Current text: Level 1 encounter cards … 31x (Expansions) … Level 4 encounter cards 40x (Expansions)
Proposed fix: (author to confirm the per-level and level-4 totals against the physical sets, or state the totals per expansion)
Rationale: Unverifiable rather than wrong; recording for completeness.

Evidence: DR p.4: 14 enemy miniatures and 7 data cards; the Mushroom Child and Mushroom Parent are separate enemies with separate data cards.
Current text: 1x Mushroom Child & Parent (Darkroot Basin)
Proposed fix: 1x Mushroom Child (Darkroot Basin) / 1x Mushroom Parent (Darkroot Basin)
Rationale: Two enemies written as one line.

Evidence: PH p.5 spells the names 'Xanthous King Jeremiah', 'Armorer Dennis', 'Marvelous Chester'. The manuscript uses 'Jeramiah' (557) and 'Jeremiah' (2492, 2528), 'Armourer Dennis', 'Marvellous Chester'.
Current text: Xanthous King Jeramiah / Armourer Dennis / Marvellous Chester
Proposed fix: Xanthous King Jeremiah / Armorer Dennis / Marvelous Chester
Rationale: Card names are proper nouns and should match the printed cards even in a British-English text; 'Jeramiah' is a misspelling in any case.

Evidence: IK p.3: 3x Titanite Scale cards; IK p.5: one Titanite Scale is added to the inventory only when every lizard in an encounter is killed before the encounter is cleared, and the icon is ignored once the three cards are gone. The manuscript awards a card per lizard killed, names it 'Titanite Chunk' at 1477 and 'Titanite Scale' at 2055, and does not say what happens when the three cards are exhausted.
Current text: award a Titanite Chunk card to any character who killed a crystal lizard during the encounter … they immediately place one Titanite Scale card into their inventory
Proposed fix: Whenever a character kills a crystal lizard, that character takes one Titanite Scale card from the supply. When no Titanite Scale cards remain, crystal lizards are no longer placed during encounter setup.
Rationale: Unifies the name with the printed card and closes the supply gap created by the per-kill award.

Evidence: 'Mastering' an encounter is used once and never defined; the resolution rules (1307–1341) know only 'cleared' and 'failed'.
Current text: The character who dropped them by successfully clearing or mastering the encounter on which they were dropped can reclaim dropped souls.
Proposed fix: A character reclaims dropped souls by surviving a clear of the encounter on whose tile the souls lie.
Rationale: Removes an undefined term; the intended rule is already stated at 1311.

Evidence: Core p.12 names left-hand and right-hand slots; the manuscript's Equipment Slots section names only 'the weapon slots' but the parry rule requires a shield in the 'left weapon slot' and the riposte uses the 'right weapon slot'.
Current text: Characters must be equipped with a shield as their left weapon … using any attack option on the weapon equipped to the right weapon slot
Proposed fix: The two weapon slots are the left-hand slot and the right-hand slot. A card equipped in either slot is in hand.
Rationale: Parry and riposte cannot be applied without named slots.

Evidence: Core p.8 lays four tiles around the bonfire; the manuscript intends a straight line of bonfire, four encounter tiles and boss tile (1115, 1152) but describes it as 'a two by six tile grid'.
Current text: arrange them so they are connected in a two by six tile grid with the bonfire tile and mini-boss tile on opposite corners.
Proposed fix: Arrange the bonfire tile, the four encounter tiles and the mini-boss tile in a straight line, with the bonfire tile and the mini-boss tile at opposite ends.
Rationale: The later text (1152) confirms the linear layout.

Evidence: No component called 'mega-boss Items' exists in the manuscript or in BDK/EC p.4; the official level 4 encounter rewards 8 souls per character (BDK/EC p.8) and no treasure.
Current text: Shuffle mega-boss Items and deal one face-down to the encounter tile.
Proposed fix: Deal one tier two treasure card per character face down to the level 4 encounter tile.
Rationale: Brings the level 4 tile into line with the manuscript's own pre-dealt treasure rule (1135, 1163); alternatively the step is deleted.

Evidence: Core p.12 modifiers add or subtract from 'the die roll'. HE p.9 'Choose any two rolled dice' is silent on modifiers. Under the manuscript's two-highest-dice rule it is unstated whether a card's fixed block modifier applies after the two dice are selected.
Current text: Determine the defence total by adding the number of sword pips on the highest two dice results. Additional dice beyond the two with the highest shown face value are ignored.
Proposed fix: The defence total is the sum of the two highest dice results plus any fixed modifiers on the equipment used.
Rationale: Closes a gap created by combining the 1E modifier rule with the HE dice cap.

Evidence: Upgrade spells are attached 'as a main action similar to casting an attack spell'; the Character Turn lists Attack as the only offensive major action, so it is unstated whether attaching an upgrade spell consumes the attack action and whether a stamina cost applies.
Current text: Instead, upgrade spells are attached to a character's equipment as a main action similar to casting an attack spell.
Proposed fix: Attaching an upgrade spell is an attack action: the character pays the stamina cost printed on the spell and makes no other attack with that catalyst this turn.
Rationale: Original mechanic with no official parallel; needs an action cost.

Evidence: Core p.19 and HE p.6 both restore all health after a victory; the manuscript's partial heal is original and is stated as one damage cube at 1347 but 'two damage' at 2043.
Current text: Remove one damage cube from each character. … they proceed to recover all stamina and two damage normally.
Proposed fix: Characters who survive to clear an encounter remove one damage cube and all stamina cubes.
Rationale: One value must be chosen; the author decides which was playtested.

Evidence: Enemy scaling is additive (+1 health per extra character, 1523); the invader rule says invaders 'do not multiply their health by the number of characters'.
Current text: Invaders do not multiply their health by the number of characters like other enemy models.
Proposed fix: Invaders do not receive enemy scaling.
Rationale: Aligns wording with the scaling rule.

Evidence: Two tie-break rules for an undecided chest treasure: random character (964) and the aggro holder (1461).
Current text: If they cannot decide, the treasure should be awarded to a randomly selected character. … the treasure will be awarded to the character who ended the encounter with the aggro token.
Proposed fix: If the players cannot agree, the treasure is awarded to the character holding the aggro token.
Rationale: One rule; the aggro version is used twice (1461, 1479).

Location: manuscript.md 1906 (Resting at The Bonfire) vs 1224 (Death & Hollowing)
Evidence: 'Lost' characters 'removed from play due to dying while hollow' are revived by resting, but 1224 says a hollow death forces an immediate rest, so no character is ever 'lost' between encounters; the term is undefined.
Current text: Resting at the bonfire also revives lost characters who have been removed from play due to dying while hollow.
Proposed fix: Resting at the bonfire revives every dead character.
Rationale: Removes an undefined status; the forced rest already covers the case.

Evidence: Core p.11 and V2 p.8 call the character value 'taunt level' and the enemy value 'threat level'. The manuscript uses 'threat' for both, so 'higher threat level' at 1690 (copied from Core p.24 'higher Taunt level') now reads as an enemy statistic.
Current text: 7. Threat Level … the enemy moves towards the character with the higher threat level.
Proposed fix: Characters have a taunt level; enemies have a threat level. (Restore 'taunt' at 745, 1003, 1275, 1277, 1289, 1690, 1694, 2192, 3056, 3058.)
Rationale: Avoids one word meaning two different statistics; optional if the author prefers a single term and defines it.

Evidence: Core p.19 uses the First Activation token to fix character order; the manuscript orders characters by threat (1289) so the token placed at 1277 is never consulted.
Current text: Place the first player token on the character with the highest threat value.
Proposed fix: (delete step 9; see D-019)
Rationale: Vestige of the 1E activation system.

Evidence: Treasure cards are dealt face down to each tile at setup, but the reward rules say characters 'draw' from the tier deck and never refer back to the dealt cards.
Current text: Deal one tier one treasure per character face-down to each encounter tile. … Draw cards from the Tier one treasure deck before defeating the mini-boss
Proposed fix: On the first clear of an encounter each character takes one of the treasure cards dealt to that tile at setup.
Rationale: Links the setup step to the reward it exists for.
